title: Psychology of the Unconscious
author: Carl Gustav Jung
translator: Beatrice M. Hinkle, 1916 (public domain, Project Gutenberg #65903)
blurb: The book that split Jung from Freud: myths, dreams and symbols as the deep, shared language of the human mind.

unconscious.m: The part of the mind we are not aware of.
unconscious.e: Her unconscious fear of dogs showed in her dreams.

persona.m: The public 'mask' or role we show the world.
persona.e: His office persona is cheerful; at home he is quiet.

strata.m: Layers, one on top of another.
strata.e: The cliff shows strata of rock from different ages.

stratum.m: Layers, one on top of another.
stratum.e: The cliff shows strata of rock from different ages.

cards.title: Dreams are ancient
cards.text: Jung starts with history: humans have always believed dreams mean something, from Egypt to the Bible's Joseph. He wants to explain why.
cards.quote: The dream interpretations of the Egyptians and Chaldeans, and the story of Joseph who interpreted Pharaoh's dreams, are known to every one
cards.qMean: People have interpreted dreams since ancient times.
cards.qLife: Grandparents who still ask 'what did you dream?' at breakfast.
cards.cap: Poussin, Joseph Interprets Pharaoh's Dream · public domain

cards.title: Layers of the soul
cards.text: Jung proposes that the mind has layers, like rock. The deepest layer is the unconscious, and it is old — shared with our ancestors.
cards.quote: the soul possesses in some degree historical strata, the oldest stratum of which would correspond to the unconscious.
cards.qMean: The mind has layers; the deepest, oldest one is the unconscious.
cards.qLife: A sudden fear of the dark that feels older than you.
cards.cap: Geological map showing rock strata · public domain

cards.title: Myths speak for everyone
cards.text: A myth is not a record of real events; it carries a thought common to all humanity, told again in new form.
cards.quote: It does not set forth any account of the old events, but rather acts in such a way that it always reveals a thought common to humanity, and once more rejuvenated.
cards.qMean: Myths express shared human ideas, renewed in every age.
cards.qLife: Superhero films retell the old hero myths for today.

cards.title: Sun father, moon mother
cards.text: The ancients saw the sun as a great father and the moon as a fruitful mother. Jung finds these images still alive in modern dreams.
cards.quote: The naïve man of antiquity saw in the sun the great Father of the heaven and the earth, and in the moon the fruitful good Mother.
cards.qMean: Ancient people saw the sun as a father and the moon as a mother.
cards.qLife: Calling the moon 'Chanda Mama' in children's songs.
cards.cap: Emblema XXV. DRACO non moritur, nisi cum fratre & sorore sua interficiatur, qui sunt Sol & Luna. - DPLA - 1e3938492016f0545f4b87f717398f38 · public domain

cards.title: The actor's mask
cards.text: Jung's word for the face we show society is persona — Latin for an actor's mask. We often mistake the mask for ourselves.
cards.quote: The term persona is really an excellent one, for persona was originally the mask which an actor wore
cards.qMean: 'Persona' comes from the actor's mask — the role we play in public.
cards.qLife: The cheerful 'work voice' you use on the phone.
cards.qBy: C. G. Jung, Collected Papers on Analytical Psychology (1916)
cards.cap: Pompeii - Theatre Mask - MAN · public domain

cards.title: Everything is you
cards.text: In Jung's view, every person and object in a dream can be a part of the dreamer.
cards.quote: The whole dream is the dreamer
cards.qMean: Every part of your dream represents part of you.
cards.qLife: Dreaming of a lost child may be about a neglected part of yourself.
cards.qBy: C. G. Jung, Collected Papers on Analytical Psychology (1916)
